issues.legal_issue: A request to bring a deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives on record may be treated as a request to set aside abatement of the entire suit, even when it expressly concerns only that plaintiff.
material_facts: Three purchasers jointly sued for specific performance of an agreement to sell.
One plaintiff died while the suit was pending.
The deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives applied to be brought on record and sought condonation of delay and setting aside of abatement only as to the deceased plaintiff.
The trial judge found sufficient cause for the delay, set aside the abatement as to the deceased plaintiff, and allowed the legal representatives to be brought on record.
The Division Bench treated the suit as having abated in its entirety because the surviving plaintiffs had not separately sought to set aside abatement.
issues.conclusion: The application and the order allowing it had the effect of setting aside abatement of the suit in its entirety; the suit was revived with the legal representatives on record.
issues.legal_principle: Abatement provisions must be construed strictly because abatement denies a hearing on the merits, while applications to set aside abatement should be considered liberally. An application to bring legal representatives on record may in substance include a request to set aside abatement, and an application concerning one plaintiff may be construed as seeking relief for the entire suit. The Court applied Order 22 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and rejected an unduly technical approach.

rule.if: death_in_multi_plaintiff_suit and (representatives_seek_substitution or representatives_brought_on_record) and delay_found_sufficient

predicates.death_in_multi_plaintiff_suit: One plaintiff died while a suit brought by multiple plaintiffs was pending.
predicates.representatives_seek_substitution: The deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives applied to be brought on record in the suit.
predicates.representatives_brought_on_record: The court allowed the deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives to be brought on record.
predicates.delay_found_sufficient: The court found sufficient cause for the delay in applying to bring the legal representatives on record.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff dies in a suit brought by multiple plaintiffs and the legal representatives seek substitution or are brought on record after the delay is found sufficient, the suit’s abatement is treated as set aside in its entirety.

issues.legal_issue: A superior court should not ordinarily interfere with a trial court’s supported finding that sufficient cause exists to condone delay and set aside abatement.
material_facts: The trial judge found sufficient cause for the delay in applying to bring the deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives on record and to set aside abatement.
The finding was reasonably reached on the material available.
The Division Bench did not reverse the finding on sufficient cause, but set aside the trial judge’s order on a separate technical ground.
issues.conclusion: The trial judge’s finding on sufficient cause was not open to interference in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: A trial judge’s finding on sufficient cause under Order 22 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, deserves weight and will not normally be disturbed when reasonably based on the available material.

predicates.appeal_from_delay_and_abatement_order: A superior court is hearing an appeal concerning an order condoning delay and setting aside abatement.
predicates.trial_court_found_sufficient_cause: The trial court found sufficient cause for the delay in seeking relief from abatement.
predicates.finding_reasonably_supported_by_record: The trial court’s finding was reasonably based on the material available.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning delay and abatement, a reasonably supported trial-court finding of sufficient cause is not ordinarily disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: Bringing a deceased party’s legal representatives on record in an appeal arising from a suit also brings them on record for the suit.
material_facts: An appeal concerning an interim injunction in the suit was pending when one plaintiff died.
The defendants who had filed that appeal applied to bring the deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives on record as respondents in the appeal.
The legal representatives also applied to be brought on record in the suit, and their application was not opposed by the co-plaintiffs.

The Court reasoned that allowing the defendants’ application in the appeal would bring the legal representatives on record for the suit as well, making the later delay in applying in the suit immaterial.
issues.conclusion: If the application to bring the legal representatives on record in the related appeal is allowed, their addition enures to the benefit of the suit as well, and a later application in the suit is unnecessary for that purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Bringing legal representatives on record at any stage of proceedings enures to the benefit of the entire proceedings; an order allowing substitution in an appeal arising from a suit has effect in the suit as well.

predicates.related_appeal_pending: An appeal arising from the suit was pending when a party died.
predicates.defendants_seek_substitution_in_appeal: The defendants who brought the related appeal applied to bring the deceased party’s legal representatives on record in that appeal.
predicates.substitution_application_allowed: The court allowed the application to bring the legal representatives on record in the appeal.

issues.definition: When defendants seek and obtain substitution in a pending appeal arising from a suit, the legal representatives are treated as on record for the suit too.

issues.legal_issue: An intra-court appeal is not maintainable against an order setting aside abatement and allowing substitution when the order decides no merits or valuable rights between the parties.
material_facts: The Division Bench entertained an intra-court appeal against the trial judge’s order condoning delay, setting aside abatement, and bringing the deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives on record.
The trial judge’s order restored the constitution of the suit so it could proceed to a determination on the merits.
The order did not decide the merits of the dispute or determine a valuable right between the parties.
Section 104 read with Order 43 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides an appeal against refusal to set aside abatement or dismissal, but not against an order granting that relief.
issues.conclusion: The Letters Patent appeal against the order setting aside abatement and allowing substitution was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Shah Babulal Khimji v. Behan D. Kangro, an order is a ‘judgment’ for Letters Patent purposes only if it decides a matter of moment or affects vital and valuable rights; an order setting aside abatement or allowing substitution merely reopens the controversy and is procedural. The Court agreed with Nurul Hoda v. Amir Hasan, Smt. Chando Devi v. Municipal Committee, Delhi, and Maria Flaviana Almeida v. Ramchandra Santuram Asavie. It also applied Section 104 and Order 43 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, under which an appeal is available from refusal to set aside abatement or dismissal, but not from an order granting that relief.

predicates.intra_court_appeal_against_procedural_or: A party brings an intra-court appeal against a procedural order made in a suit.
predicates.order_sets_aside_abatement_or_allows_sub: The challenged order sets aside abatement or allows a deceased party’s legal representatives to be brought on record.
predicates.order_decides_no_merits_or_valuable_righ: The order does not determine the merits of the dispute or decide a valuable right between the parties.

issues.definition: An intra-court appeal is not maintainable when it challenges an order that sets aside abatement or allows substitution without determining the merits or valuable rights.
